This log requires the technical pages to be detailed enough for someone to re-implement the
code from them. Writing those pages for the first time found a bug in the IMAS export.

## What was wrong

Every code in this project gives radial position as a normalised radius from 0 to 1. IMAS, the
fusion data standard we use at the code's boundaries, also requires the radius in metres. The
conversion multiplies by the plasma's radius at the edge. There are two candidates for that
radius: the geometric half-width of the plasma, and a radius defined from the magnetic flux it
encloses. IMAS uses the second. Our export used the first.

For the circular test plasma used in M0 the two are equal, so every test passed. For shaped
plasmas they differ:

| plasma | flux radius vs half-width |
|---|---|
| ITER hybrid scenario | [a factor of 1.37]{.claim}[C-030](/Blog/toktoit/claims.qmd#c-030){.cid .st-measured} |
| MAST-U (spherical tokamak) | [a factor of 1.52]{.claim}[C-021](/Blog/toktoit/claims.qmd#c-021){.cid .st-tested} |

Every exported equilibrium therefore had its radius in metres too small by that factor, the
derivative of the volume with respect to radius too large by the same factor, and one
geometric average off by its square.

## Why the tests did not catch it

The adapter test converts data to IMAS and back and checks that nothing changed. It passed to
fourteen decimal places. The import used the same wrong radius as the export, so the two errors
cancelled exactly. A round-trip test shows that two functions are inverses of each other; it
does not show that the data in between matches the standard's definitions.

## How it was found, and the fix

Writing the conversion as an equation, with each symbol defined, showed that the two radii are
different quantities. The fix stores the flux radius explicitly in the equilibrium. New tests
compare the exported value with each source code's own value, not with our import. They agree
to [10^−12^]{.claim}[C-033](/Blog/toktoit/claims.qmd#c-033){.cid .st-tested}. This comparison does not depend on our import code, and would have
failed from the start.

No published result depended on the exported values: the simulation used the correct quantities
internally. The same review found a related issue in the inputs the guard checks, which has
gone to the owner as a modelling decision ([OQ-10](/Blog/toktoit/decisions.qmd#oq-10)).

**Where this stands**: M1 in progress.
